findings.documented: API key is sent as a query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: API key must be sent as a request header: X-API-Key: IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX.
findings.how_found: first API call using the documented query parameter method returned an error with explicit instructions to use the header instead
findings.impact: every request must use the X-API-Key header; the documented method fails on all endpoints
evidence: Using a query parameter returns {"detail": "send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter"}

findings.documented: Login response has field 'token', expires_in 86400 (24h), user object contains 'name', and 'there is no refresh flow'
findings.actual: Login response field is 'access_token' (not 'token'), expires_in is 900 (15min), user object has no 'name' field, and a refresh flow exists via 'refresh_token'
findings.how_found: called POST /auth/login and compared the actual response structure against the documented one, then tested POST /auth/refresh with the returned refresh_token
findings.impact: frontend must use 'access_token' field, implement token refresh every 15 minutes via /auth/refresh, and cannot rely on a user 'name' field

findings.documented: POST /auth/logout invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: Tokens are stateless and discarded on client side. Discarded tokens remain valid until expiry (15 min) and refresh tokens until their expiry (7 days), even after logout is called
findings.how_found: called POST /auth/logout, observed the response note about stateless tokens, then verified by using the 'discarded' access_token on GET /v1/listings (still worked), waiting for access_token expiry, and using the 'discarded' refresh_token on POST /auth/refresh (still generated new tokens)
findings.impact: logout is client-side only — clear tokens from storage. No server-side revocation exists. Refresh tokens remain usable for 7 days from issue regardless of logout
evidence: Logout returns {"ok": true, "note": "tokens are stateless; discard them client side"}

findings.documented: Returns only active sale listings; inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side. Listing object does not include an is_live field
findings.actual: Returns all listings including inactive ones. Each listing has an is_live boolean field indicating whether it is currently active.
findings.how_found: fetched listings and observed an undocumented is_live field in every listing object, with some listings having is_live: false — contradicting the claim that inactive listings are excluded
findings.impact: frontend must filter listings by is_live: true before displaying to users. Total record count from the endpoint includes inactive listings

findings.documented: Pagination uses page (1-indexed, default 1) and limit (default 20, max 200). Response contains total, page, page_size, results
findings.actual: Pagination uses offset (0-indexed, default 0) and limit (default 20, max 50). Response contains limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results. There is no page parameter
findings.how_found: fetched /v1/listings and observed the response shape uses offset/count/has_more instead of page/page_size. Tested limit=200 which saturated at 50
findings.impact: all collection endpoints must use offset-based pagination with limit capped at 50. Frontend must increment offset by limit to paginate, or use has_more to know when to stop

findings.documented: Query parameters furnishing, min_price, and max_price are supported as filters on /v1/listings
findings.actual: These three parameters are accepted but silently ignored — they do not filter results. Only offset, limit, locality, bhk, property_type, sort_by, and order actually work
findings.how_found: tested each documented query parameter individually and compared results. furnishing, min_price, and max_price returned the same unfiltered results regardless of value
findings.impact: price range and furnishing filtering must be done client-side

findings.actual: The correct path is GET /v1/listings/{listing_id} (plural). The singular /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns {"detail": "Not Found"}
findings.how_found: called GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} as documented and received a 404. Tried the plural form /v1/listings/{listing_id} which worked
findings.impact: frontend must use /v1/listings/{listing_id} for detail pages

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings
findings.actual: This endpoint does not exist. No alternate routes found for this functionality
findings.how_found: called GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar and received a 404. Tried alternate paths — none exist
findings.impact: similar listings functionality must be implemented client-side using available listing data

findings.documented: Only /v1/listing/{listing_id} (singular) is documented for fetching a single listing
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id} (plural) exists and returns a single listing. This is the working endpoint, but it is not in the documentation
findings.how_found: discovered while testing the documented singular path which returned 404 — tried the plural form and it worked
findings.impact: this is the correct endpoint to use for listing detail pages

findings.documented: Supports page, limit, locality, bhk, furnishing, sort_by, order — filters listed inline without detail, sort_by options not specified
findings.actual: Supports offset (not page), limit, locality, bhk, furnishing, sort_by, order. sort_by accepts: price, deposit, posted_at, bedroom, carpet_area
findings.how_found: tested all filter parameters on /v1/rentals. Confirmed page does not exist (uses offset like listings). Tested sort_by with various field names to determine which are accepted
findings.impact: frontend must use offset-based pagination for rentals and can sort by deposit and carpet_area in addition to the obvious fields
